sources.passages: Efron and Tibshirani (1985), pp. 16 and 23, equations 7.1–7.2
sources.scope: Resample joint observations as units; percentile interval endpoints. Application to matched model responses is the study implementation. The earlier 1993 book download is only an 11-page introductory excerpt.

Exact conditional McNemar uses discordant pairs and a binomial null with probability 0.5. Its conservatism is explicitly reported. Authors prefer other variants; citation does not imply they recommend the exact test.

sources.passages: Benjamini and Hochberg (1995), pp. 291–293, equation 1 and Theorem 1
sources.scope: Original full text: FDR definition and step-up procedure; independence assumption in the theorem. Relevant pages visually read; full proof not audited.

sources.passages: Cohen (1986), Current Contents Social & Behavioral Sciences, no. 3, p. 18
sources.scope: Author retrospective explains chance-corrected agreement and a worked kappa calculation. Corroborates the report definition alongside Artstein and Poesio [56]; not a copy of Cohen (1960). Audit support only, not an added bibliography entry.

sources.passages: SAS/STAT 15.2 User’s Guide (2020), pp. 7870–7873; p. 7873 formula visually checked
sources.scope: Documents Connor normal approximation. Repository MDE uses (z_0.975 + z_0.8)*sqrt(discordance/n), simplifying alternative variance. Report now identifies approximation and unadjusted 0.05 level; does not claim exact power for BH-corrected tests.
Original text calls verbal category divisions arbitrary. Supports the report’s caution about universal categories.

Full-text conceptual TOST support: both one-sided tests, 90% interval at alpha .05, justification of bounds. Does not independently validate the study’s binary normal approximation. Post hoc status and that approximation remain explicit in section 4.6.

sources.passages: Original 1987 article, pp. 658–661; p. 661 visually checked
sources.scope: Direct original-source support for interval hypotheses, both one-sided tests at alpha and equivalence to a 1−2alpha confidence interval inside the margins. Original assumes normal observations and t tests; report appropriately labels its binary normal approximation and post hoc analysis.

sources.passages: Original 1993 book scan, printed pp. 47, 86–87, 113 and 170–171; pages visually read
sources.scope: Complete 451-page PDF obtained. Resampling with replacement, multivariate observations and preserving pairs, and percentile endpoints verified directly. The report’s matched-response bootstrap is an application of these principles. This checks relevant passages, not every page or proof in the book.
